title: Client-aborted requests trip the Redis breaker and degrade every join for 3 s
repro: Scratch test y_test.go: Guard with a store returning ctx.Err(); call Decide 20 times with an already-cancelled parent ctx (what net/http gives the handler when the client closes the connection), then Decide once with a healthy store and live ctx. Real attack: one verified account sends joins and resets the TCP connection immediately, 20 times in 1 s.
evidence: Output: 'after 20 client-aborted joins, next honest join tags: [MODE_SHADOW DEGRADED]'. observe() counts every Observe error (context.Canceled included) as DegradedRedisError and calls br.fail; BreakerN=20/1s, open 3s. While open all history rules (R1-server, R4D, R4N, R7, sticky) are skipped for every user.
fix: In observe(), if ctx.Err() != nil (parent cancelled) return the unknown state without br.fail and without counting redis_error; only count deadline/timeout from cctx or real Redis errors. Add a test with a cancelled parent ctx.

title: Breaker opens deterministically at T0 (shuffle.lua blocks Redis) and under pool pressure; no half-open
repro: By construction, not executed (needs real Redis): shuffle.lua ZADDs the whole lobby in one script at T0 on the same Redis instance, so every observe.lua EVALSHA waits > 4 ms; the antibot client has PoolSize 128 and PoolTimeout 4 ms, so >128 concurrent joins also fail fast. 20 failures within 1 s opens the breaker for 3 s, and it re-arms after each open.
evidence: redisstate/store.go NewClient (PoolTimeout=4ms, PoolSize=128); config.go BreakerN=20, BreakerOpen=3s; breaker.allow has no half-open probe. The flash-crowd moment when history rules matter most is the moment they are off, and a bot farm can time its joins to T0+.
fix: Add a half-open probe (one request through after open, close on success) and backoff, separate pool wait from the command budget, alert on the antibot degraded rate, and load-test shuffle.lua at 100k lobby with the guard enabled. Consider a separate Redis for antibot state.

title: Authenticated DeviceID is never used; R4D/R7 keyed on client-chosen fp/sq, so a bot sending {"v":1,"pe":1} scores 0
repro: Scratch x_test.go TestCombos: UA 'Mozilla/5.0 Chrome/120', body {"v":1,"pe":1}, clean state -> forged_human score=0.000 PASS. Replaying a captured human snapshot across identities: change one interval by 1 ms (new sq) or drop fp/sq/sn and R4D (needs sig.FP) and R7 (needs sig.SQ) cannot fire. grep: Input.DeviceID is not read by any rule.
evidence: rules.go:64 requires sig.FP != "" and R7 requires sig.SQ != ""; both are optional client fields. Q-1 accepts forged signals, but the only server-trusted per-device key (principal DeviceID, bound at login) is ignored, so the server-side rules R4D/R7 are optional for the attacker.
fix: Key R4D on the principal DeviceID hash (fp only as fallback when DeviceID is empty) and treat fp != DeviceID as a weak sign. Document that only R1-server, R4N, R5-UA and sticky are attacker-proof.

title: Explicit automation signs alone never BLOCK: R5 (0.80) is below the BLOCK tier (0.85)
repro: TestCombos: UA 'python-requests/2' (same for wd=true or a HeadlessChrome UA) with body {"v":1,"pe":1} -> score=0.800 action=SLOW_LANE applied=SLOW_LANE fired=[R5]. The bot gets a real slot, only P=100000 positions behind.
evidence: config.go Tiers {0.30,0.60,0.85}, weight R5=0.80. A forged pe:1 removes R3, the only rule that pushes R5 over 0.85. A self-declared python-requests UA is the strongest bot sign yet is not blocked.
fix: Make a strong non-missing R5 reach BLOCK by itself (weight >= 0.85 or force BLOCK when realStrong and payload not missing). Update corpus/golden tests.

title: Legitimate non-browser clients (okhttp, Go-http-client, axios, node-fetch) and stale bundles are blocked or slow-laned; block is sticky 24 h
repro: UA 'okhttp/4.12' (an official Android app or e2e/load tool) joining with no signals: R3 (0.4) + R5 (0.8 via UA deny, strong non-missing sign so block eligible) = 0.88 >= 0.85 -> BLOCK; revoke.lua deletes the slot and sets ab:{ev}:blk:{id} for 24 h. A browser running an old cached bundle (no body): TestCombos no_body score=0.880 SLOW_LANE tag CAPPED. The okhttp BLOCK is derived from rules.go, not executed.
evidence: DefaultUADeny includes okhttp, Go-http-client, axios/, node-fetch; rules.go:73 realStrong via uaDenied; the blk key has no unblock path (revoke.lua SET EX 86400, nothing deletes it).
fix: Remove okhttp/axios/node-fetch/Go-http-client from the deny list or make them weak signs; add a first-party client bypass; add an operator command to clear ab:{ev}:blk:{id}; call out in the runbook that shadow mode must be reviewed for these before enforce.

title: One rule (R4D, 0.60) lands exactly on the SLOW_LANE lower bound; shared device or reused sessionStorage snapshot demotes humans
repro: TestCombos R4D_alone: FPIdentities=4, pe=3 -> score=0.600 SLOW_LANE. Real path: family/kiosk browser with 4 accounts logging in within 5 min (fp lives in localStorage). The snapshot is stored per event in sessionStorage and not cleared on logout, so account B in the same tab sends account A's snapshot (same sq and fp): 3 accounts fire R7, 4 fire R4D+R7 = 0.80 SLOW_LANE.
evidence: tier() uses >= with Tiers[1]=0.60 and R4D=0.60; antibot-signals.ts clearSignals runs only on PAID/SOLD_OUT.
fix: Set R4D below 0.60 alone (e.g. 0.55) so it needs a second sign, and clear ef:ab:* on logout or bind the stored snapshot to the identity id.

title: Slow joiners arriving between T0 and shuffle jump ahead of pre-T0 slow lobby members (P-13 not held in that window)
repro: Scratch miniredis test lane_test.go: 5 slow lobby joins before T0 (pre1..5), sale_start moved into the past, 2 slow joins (late, late2) before shuffle runs, then shuffle.lua. Queue order by score-1e12: tlate 100001, tp1 100001, tlate2 100002, tp2 100002, tp3 100003, tp4 100004, tp5 100005. late2 precedes tp3..tp5, and ties break by token.
evidence: join.lua adds slow_lottery_size = 0 before shuffle, so score = 1e12+seq+P; shuffle.lua then places lobby members at 1e12+P+i, interleaving with early-seq late joiners.
fix: Give pre-shuffle post-T0 slow joiners an offset above any possible m (for example P + a fixed upper bound), or re-score them inside shuffle.lua after placing the slow lobby. Add the interleaving case to lane_integration_test.

title: Held keys (keydown auto-repeat) enter iv as constant intervals and fire R1 for keyboard-only humans
repro: TestCombos keyrepeat_R1: ke=30, iv=[33,33,34,33,33,33,34,33,33] (holding Tab/ArrowDown) -> R1 fires, score 0.500 (CHALLENGE, passes); with a shared-device R4D it is 0.800 SLOW_LANE.
evidence: onKeyDown records every keydown with no event.repeat check; iv keeps the last 32 so a long hold fills it.

title: Network prefix stored in clear in Redis keys and bot_decisions; per-identity 24 h block key
repro: Run a join with an IPv4 client: keys ab:{ev}:net:203.0.113.0/24 and ab:{ev}:nj:203.0.113.0/24:<minute> appear (10 min TTL); bot_decisions.ip stores the same prefix. Identity UUID is in ab:{ev}:blk:{id} for 24 h. Derived from Keys() and toRow(), not run against Redis.
evidence: store.go Keys() builds net:+net.String(); bot_decisions.go toRow sets ip=NetPrefix.String(). fp is HMAC'd but the network prefix is not. No retention job for bot_decisions seen.
fix: HMAC the prefix with the same key for keys and the DB column, and add a retention policy for bot_decisions.

title: No-finding: payload hardening and Decide latency held under hostile 4 KiB inputs
repro: Scratch TestPerf, 2000 Decide calls each with nil store: about 800 unknown keys (4001 B), 2000-level nested array under an unknown key (4012 B), 600 unicode escapes plus a 64-char invalid zone, and {"pe":1e999,"rt":-5,"se":NaN,"ke":-1,"iv":[1e400]}.
evidence: avg 227 us / 110 us / 134 us / 3 us; worst single call 1.7 ms (cold); no panic and no refused join; NaN/Inf/negative fields become absent. join.lua stays idempotent for an existing slot and re-join with a slot yields REJOIN/PASS. Gateway Rewrite overwrites X-Forwarded-For, so the first element is not client-forgeable.
fix: None. Optionally add the many-keys payload to the benchmark; 227 us per join is about 2.3 cores at 10k joins/s.
